sections.title: Settings
sections.description: Acquisition settings files: one JSON document with the device, the laser program, the experiment and the run. Load one from the workspace (drop a settings file onto ChiSurf), recover them from a measurement, or save what is set now.

sections.label: From
sections.description: A settings file (⚙) or a measurement (⏱) of the workspace. Settings files enter ChiSurf through the drop, like every input.

buttons.label: Load
buttons.description: Read the chosen settings file, fill the form and send it to the connected device and laser. The laser's emission stays off.

buttons.label: Use settings of this measurement
buttons.description: Recover the settings of the chosen measurement from its file header. What the header did not record is listed in the tooltip of the line below.

buttons.label: Use its windows
buttons.description: Take the micro-time windows the measurement's laser program implies into the Experiment setup.

buttons.label: Save as…
buttons.description: Write what the form, the device and the laser hold now to a settings file.

sections.label: Mode
sections.description: Point: a single-molecule measurement at one spot -- bursts, E-S and the running trace. FCS: a point measurement for fluorescence correlation -- the correlation curve builds up live. Image: a scan -- the image builds up line by line from the scanner's markers, with fast-FLIM maps.

sections.label: Source
sections.description: Where the photons come from: the simulator (a MultiHarp measuring a PIE smFRET sample with a known answer — its records go through the same device path as a real measurement), a photon stream from the Datasets workspace played back at measurement speed, or a PicoQuant device connected over USB.

sections.label: Excitation
sections.description: How the simulated sample is excited: PIE (a green and a red pulse per period, so stoichiometry is measured) or two colour (the green laser only).

sections.label: Population 1: E
sections.description: FRET efficiency of the first simulated population. Each molecule carries donor and acceptor; its photons are split into donor and acceptor channel by this E.

sections.label: Population 2: E
sections.description: FRET efficiency of the second simulated population.

sections.label: Stoichiometry S
sections.description: Stoichiometry of both populations: the share of donor-excited photons in all photons of a molecule (0.5 = equally bright under both lasers).

sections.label: Concentration
sections.description: Molecules of each population in the simulation box. Higher means more bursts per second, and more coincident molecules.

sections.title: Simulated FCS sample
sections.description: One freely diffusing dye under the green laser, so the FCS fit has a known answer: the number of molecules in the focus and the diffusion coefficient (diffusion time = w0² / 4D).

sections.label: Molecules in focus N
sections.description: Mean number of molecules in the focal volume (the inverse amplitude of the correlation curve).

sections.label: D (µm²/s)
sections.description: Diffusion coefficient of the dye; with the simulated focus it sets the diffusion time.

sections.label: Brightness (kHz)
sections.description: Photons per millisecond of one molecule at the focus centre.

sections.label: Seed
sections.description: Seeds diffusion and emission, so a run is reproducible.

sections.label: Photon stream
sections.description: A photons dataset of the Datasets workspace, played back at measurement speed. Drop the file on the ChiSurf window to add it.

sections.label: Speed
sections.description: How fast simulated or replayed photons arrive: 1 is the pace of the real measurement, 10 ten times faster.

sections.label: Preset
sections.description: Realistic: what a confocal smFRET measurement shows (donor-/acceptor-only molecules, bleaching, blinking, crosstalk, background, IRF, dead time). Ideal: everything off — the clean stream for teaching and exact tests. Editing a value makes it Custom.

sections.label: Donor-only
sections.description: Fraction of molecules without an active acceptor: an island at stoichiometry ≈ 1 and E ≈ 0.

sections.label: Acceptor-only
sections.description: Fraction of molecules without a donor: an island at stoichiometry ≈ 0.

sections.label: Aggregates
sections.description: Fraction of bright, slowly diffusing particles: rare bright spikes and long bursts.

sections.label: Brightness spread
sections.description: Molecule-to-molecule brightness spread (coefficient of variation): broadens burst sizes and the clusters.

sections.label: Diffusion (µm²/s)
sections.description: Translational diffusion coefficient; with the focus it sets the burst duration (80 µm²/s ≈ a 30 kDa protein).

sections.label: γ
sections.description: Detection-efficiency × quantum-yield ratio of acceptor to donor. γ ≠ 1 shifts raw E; the corrected E uses it.

sections.label: α (leakage)
sections.description: Donor emission leaking into the acceptor channel: raises raw E, most visibly for donor-only molecules.

sections.label: δ (direct exc.)
sections.description: Direct excitation of the acceptor by the donor laser (relative to its own laser): raises raw E.

sections.label: Donor lifetime (ns)
sections.description: Donor lifetime without FRET; a FRET population decays with τ_D (1 − E).

sections.label: Acceptor lifetime (ns)
sections.description: Acceptor lifetime: decay of the directly excited acceptor and the delay of sensitised emission.

sections.label: IRF FWHM (ns)
sections.description: Instrument response width, with a small exponential tail and per-detector timing jitter.

sections.label: Background donor (kHz)
sections.description: Uncorrelated background of the donor detector (dark counts, ambient light), flat in micro time.

sections.label: Background acceptor (kHz)
sections.description: Uncorrelated background of the acceptor detector.

sections.label: Scatter (kHz)
sections.description: Scattered and Raman light of the donor laser in the donor detector: prompt window, instrument response only.

sections.label: Afterpulsing
sections.description: Probability that a detection repeats on the same detector shortly after (detector afterpulsing).

sections.label: Dead time (ns)
sections.description: Detector dead time: a photon arriving within it after another is lost (count-rate saturation).

sections.label: Acceptor bleaching (/ms)
sections.description: Acceptor photobleaching rate at the focus centre: bursts end as donor only — tails towards high S and low E.

sections.label: Donor bleaching (/ms)
sections.description: Donor photobleaching rate at the focus centre: bursts end as acceptor only — tails towards low S.

sections.label: Acceptor blinking (/ms)
sections.description: Rate into the acceptor's dark state (it returns after ~0.2 ms): FRET drops for a while within a burst.

sections.label: Drift (per min)
sections.description: Slow relative intensity change per minute (focus, laser power, evaporation).

sections.label: Device
sections.description: The TCSPC devices connected (PicoQuant MultiHarp, PicoHarp 330, HydraHarp 500 over USB; Becker & Hickl SPC cards over PCI), driven natively by libphacq. Connect opens and initialises it (PicoQuant: T3 mode, B&H: FIFO mode).

buttons.label: Connect
buttons.description: Open and initialise the device and show its identity, count rates and every setting it has. Nothing is recorded until Start.

buttons.label: Disconnect
buttons.description: Release the device so another program can use it.

sections.description: Every setting of the connected device, as its driver describes it: sync, each input on its own panel, timing, markers. An edit is sent to the device at once (between runs); a value the device refuses is named here and the panel shows the device's values again.

sections.title: Laser
sections.description: The pulsed laser driver (PicoQuant Sepia II, or a simulated one). Connecting switches every output off; a program reaches the laser only with Apply, and emission needs Emission on after that.

sections.label: Laser
sections.description: Auto uses the Sepia II driver when its library is installed, else the simulated laser. Why Sepia II is not available is shown on the status line.

buttons.label: Connect
buttons.description: Open the laser. All outputs are switched off.

buttons.label: Disconnect
buttons.description: Switch the outputs off and release the laser.

buttons.label: Laser off
buttons.description: Block all emission now. Always available; never fails.

sections.description: The connected laser driver's own controls: per laser head the pulsed / continuous switch, the repetition rate (its own oscillator or an external trigger) and the intensity; the soft lock switches all outputs. Changes reach the laser at once.

sections.title: Program
sections.description: What Apply sends to the laser. Any change switches the outputs off until Apply.

columns.title: On
columns.tooltip: Whether the head's sequencer output fires.

sections.label: Divider
sections.description: The oscillator's base frequency is divided by this to give the pulse rate the sequencer distributes.

sections.title: Sequencer
sections.description: Pulses per output in one sequence, which outputs fire and which give the sync.

columns.title: Pulses
columns.tooltip: Pulses of this output in one sequence (0: not in the sequence).

columns.title: Sync
columns.tooltip: The output contributes to the sync signal.

buttons.label: Apply
buttons.description: Send the program to the laser. Emission stays off.

buttons.label: Emission on
buttons.description: Allow emission. Offered only after Apply.

buttons.label: Windows from laser
buttons.description: Use the micro-time windows the applied program implies (one per enabled excitation, shifted by the sync offset) in the Experiment setup.

sections.label: Instrument setup
sections.description: Which detector is donor and which acceptor, and the excitation windows: a setup row of the Datasets workspace (drop a detector setup JSON on the window), or the default for the measurement type — routing channel 0 donor, 1 acceptor; PIE splits the laser period into prompt and delay halves. A setup with gamma, beta, alpha and delta gives corrected FRET efficiency and stoichiometry.

sections.label: Measurement type
sections.description: How the setup is read: single colour, two colour, PIE, µs-ALEX, MFD or three-colour PIE. 'From the setup' takes the type the setup describes. The type decides the quantities (proximity ratio, stoichiometry, anisotropy), the live histograms and which quality checks apply.
The setup as read: detectors, windows and whether E and S are corrected. Hover for the details.

sections.label: Alternation period (µs)
sections.description: µs-ALEX only: the laser alternation period; the first half excites the donor, the second the acceptor.

sections.label: Minimum photons
sections.description: A burst needs at least this many photons (L).

sections.label: Window photons
sections.description: The sliding window: this many consecutive photons (m) ...

sections.label: Window time (ms)
sections.description: ... arriving within this time (T) belong to a burst. The same criterion as Burst Selection's sliding-window search, so the run can be re-analysed offline with identical bursts.

sections.label: Span (s)
sections.description: How many seconds the running trace shows: the most recent ones, scrolling. Default 1 s.

sections.label: Bin (ms)
sections.description: Bin width of the running trace. Default 1 ms (bursts last a few ms).
The scan of the replayed file, read from its header (ImgHdr tags).

sections.label: Pixels x
sections.description: Pixels per line.

sections.label: Pixels y
sections.description: Lines per frame.

sections.label: Width (µm)
sections.description: The scanned width; a pixel is width / pixels wide.

sections.label: Height (µm)
sections.description: The scanned height.

sections.label: Dwell (ms)
sections.description: Time on one pixel. A line takes pixels x dwell; the line rate follows.

sections.label: Frames
sections.description: Frames per plane; their photons add up in the live image.

sections.label: Bidirectional
sections.description: Odd lines are scanned right to left (faster; needs a well-aligned scanner).

sections.label: Z planes
sections.description: Planes of a z stack (1: one plane).

sections.label: Z step (µm)
sections.description: Distance between the planes of a z stack.

sections.label: Beads
sections.description: Bright beads on the dim outline of a cell; half of them with each lifetime.

sections.label: τ₁ (ns)
sections.description: Lifetime of the first bead kind (mostly on detector 0).

sections.label: τ₂ (ns)
sections.description: Lifetime of the second bead kind (mostly on detector 1).

sections.label: Brightness
sections.description: Photon rate of one emitter at the focus centre (a bead is a few emitters). Too bright piles up: watch the Pile-up light.

sections.label: Duration (s)
sections.description: Stop after this much measurement time; 0 measures until you press Stop.

sections.label: Name
sections.description: The recording's name: its file in the project's recordings folder and its row in Datasets.

sections.label: Store photons
sections.description: Embed (default): the photons are stored inside the project's .cs.pto when the run stops, so the project carries its data. Link: the project records the file's path and checksum only. Written beside the project while measuring, so a crash leaves the photons on disk.

buttons.label: Load example
buttons.description: Choose the simulator with two populations of known E (0.2 and 0.8, S 0.5) and the default PIE setup, ready to Start.

buttons.label: Start
buttons.description: Start measuring: photons are analysed live and written to the recording as they arrive.

buttons.label: Stop
buttons.description: Stop measuring. The open burst is closed, the recording finished, and both enter the project: the photons as a dataset, its bursts as a run below it.

sections.description: What the run is doing, and where it was saved (hover for the full path).

sections.label: Histogram
sections.description: Which of the measurement type's histograms to show: E–S (with its marginals) for PIE and ALEX, the proximity ratio for two colour, anisotropy and proximity ratio for MFD, burst size and duration for a single colour.
The selected histogram of the bursts, building up live (2-D with both marginals).

sections.label: Map
sections.description: Which map: intensity (all detectors), mean arrival time (fast FLIM), a single detector, or a micro-time window (PIE).
The image building up line by line from the scan's markers.
Point: the running smFRET trace of the last seconds -- donor up, acceptor (FRET and directly excited) down. Image: count rate per detector.
Micro-time histograms per detector, with the windows of the setup.
Traffic lights: the quality checks of the measurement type, the worst one overall. Hover a line for what it means and what to do.
